title: Stamp archive documents without moving their dates

blocks.text: The document service still writes into a legacy archive whose header stores the time a document was saved as a signed 32-bit count of seconds since 1970. Lease contracts that run to 2040 have started to show up in the archive as documents from 1903, and a scanned land deed from 1900 is filed as if it were saved in 2036.

`ArchiveStamps.header` already builds the header line. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/ArchiveStamps.java`: `toStampSeconds(epochMillis)` returns the seconds the archive stores for that time, and refuses a time the format can't hold with an `ArithmeticException`, so that no document is ever stamped with another date.

cases.says: a time the 32-bit format can hold, including its first and last second, is stamped with its exact count of seconds
a time after 2038-01-19T03:14:07Z is refused with an ArithmeticException instead of being stamped as a date in 1901 or later
a time before 1901-12-13T20:45:52Z is refused too, instead of being stamped as a date in the 2030s

origin.section: A Narrowing Integer Cast Keeps the Low Bits and Never Fails

concepts: A narrowing integer cast keeps the low-order bits and never throws, so an out-of-range value becomes another, possibly plausible, number; Math.toIntExact throws instead.
